chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Dawood al-Raqqi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'and His Throne was upon the water.' He said: 'What are they saying?' I said: 'They say that the Throne was upon the water and the Lord was above it.' So he said: 'They have lied. Whoever claims this has made God a carried one, and described Him with the attribute of a creature, and it follows that the thing carrying Him would be stronger than Him.'
I said: 'Explain it to me, may I be your sacrifice!' So he said: 'Indeed God loaded His religion and His knowledge upon the water before there was earth, sky, jinn, humans, sun, or moon.'

Then when God intended to create the creatures, He scattered them before Him and said to them: 'Who is your Lord?' The first to speak was the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and the Imams (God's blessings be upon them), and they said: 'You are our Lord.' So He loaded them with the knowledge and the religion.

Then He said to the angels: 'These are the carriers of My religion, My knowledge, and My trustees among My creation, and they are the ones who will be held accountable.' Then He said to the Children of Adam: 'Acknowledge to God the Lordship, and to these persons the wilayah and obedience.' So they said: 'Yes, our Lord, we acknowledge.'

Then God said to the angels: 'Bear witness!' So the angels said: 'We bear witness, lest they say tomorrow that we were unaware of this. Or lest you say: it was only our fathers who committed shirk before, and we were their offspring after them — so would You destroy us for what the wrongdoers did?' O Dawood! Our wilayah is confirmed upon them in the Covenant.

key_terms.الْعَرْشُ: The Throne — a Quranic concept for divine sovereignty and governance. Imam al-Sadiq here reinterprets it away from any physical-spatial meaning.
key_terms.الْمَحْمُولُ: Carried one — the Imam uses this term to show that applying physical directionality to God would reduce Him to a creature.
key_terms.الْمِيثَاقُ: The Covenant — the primordial agreement between God and all souls before creation, central to Shia theology of Imamate.
key_terms.الْوَلَايَةُ: Wilayah — guardianship, authority, and spiritual leadership of the Imams, here confirmed as an obligation binding on all humans from before creation.
key_terms.حَمَلَةُ الدِّينِ: Carriers of the religion — the Imams as the designated bearers of divine knowledge and religious authority.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'His Throne was upon the water' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses a theological question about the Quranic verse 'His Throne was upon the water' (11:7), rejecting the literalist interpretation that would imply God is physically carried or located above the Throne. The Imam explains that the 'Throne upon water' refers to God placing His religion and knowledge upon the water as a primordial trust before all of creation existed. He then reveals the cosmological event of the primordial covenant (mithaq), where God scattered the souls of all beings, asked them to acknowledge His Lordship, and the Prophet, Ali, and the Imams were the first to respond, thus being entrusted with divine knowledge and religion — an authority that was witnessed and confirmed upon all of humanity by the angels.
